Modern research speaks more cautiously: stimulating superficial and deep tissues can modify nerve pain signals and some autonomic reactions.

Alege două sisteme (de exemplu, Plămân ș: Choose two systems (for example, Lung and Kidney). For each, write in a table: the traditional function, the tissue, the associated emotion, and what modern anatomy would say about the organ of the same name. Notice where they overlap and where they differ.

Alege o linie de pe antebraț, de la înch: Choose a line on the forearm, from the wrist toward the elbow, and press gently every 2 cm with your thumb, 5 seconds each, in “line pressure” style. Breathe slowly and stop if pain appears. Do not perform forced stretching maneuvers without training.
Alege o reclamă la un aparat sau o terap: Choose an advertisement for a device or therapy and tick the warning signs: does it promise a cure for different diseases? Does it rely on testimonials? Alege o senzație banală de zi cu zi (de: Choose an everyday ordinary sensation (for example, cold hands). Note how you would describe it in each of the four Ba Gang pairs, then write three possible medical explanations that a doctor could check. Notice what the grid alone cannot tell you.
Alege o zi obișnuită și descrie-o în dou: Choose an ordinary day and describe it in two columns: “TCM language” (for example, “low Yang energy in the evening”) and “everyday language” (“I’m tired after a meal”). Alege un singur punct din listă, de exem: Choose a single point from the list, for example PC6. Locate it on your own forearm using cun (2 cun above the wrist crease, between the tendons). Do not repeat more than a few times a day, and do not use the exercise instead of medical help.
Alege un titlu de știre despre o terapie: Choose a news headline about a therapy and answer five questions: What type of study is it? Who was compared with whom? How many participants? Apasă blând-mediu 60 s pe fiecare punct,: Press gently to moderately for 60 s on each point, with slow breathing, in the last 7–10 days of the cycle. Gently massage the lower abdomen (CV6); do not press painfully.
Apasă blând-mediu 60–90 s pe fiecare pun: Press gently to moderately for 60–90 s on each point, with slow breathing (4 s in, 6 s out). You can do it 1–3 times a day, especially at moments of tension.
Apasă ferm dar confortabil PC6 pe fiecar: Press PC6 firmly but comfortably on each wrist for 60–90 s, with slow breathing; then CV12 and ST36 for 30–60 s. You can also use acupressure wristbands; repeat as needed.
Apasă mediu 30–60 s la nivelul fesei și: Press moderately for 30–60 s at the buttock and the back of the leg, without pressing directly on very sensitive or numb areas. Repeat once or twice a day.
Apasă mediu 30–60 s pe punctele de pe an: Press moderately for 30–60 s on the points of the forearm and around the elbow, avoiding the most painful area at first. Repeat 1–2 times a day and combine with relative rest for the arm.
Apasă mediu 30–60 s pe punctele de pe ga: Press moderately for 30–60 s on the points of the lower leg and next to the ankles; you can massage the sole with a small ball rolled under the foot. Repeat daily, in the evening and after exertion.
Apasă mediu 30–60 s pe punctele din juru: Press moderately for 30–60 s on the points around the knee and on the lower leg, avoiding swelling or the inflamed joint. You can also apply gentle heat; repeat daily.
Apasă mediu 60–90 s pe SP6, LR3 și ST36,: Press moderately for 60–90 s on SP6, LR3 and ST36, then gently massage the lower abdomen (CV4) and the lumbar area (BL23). Start 1–2 days before menstruation and repeat 1–2 times a day. Do NOT use SP6 if you are pregnant or trying to conceive.
Apasă un element. Săgețile continue verz: Press an element. Solid green arrows = generating (Sheng); dotted red lines = controlling (Ke).
Apasă ușor LI20 și EX-HN3, apoi LI4 și G: Press LI20 and EX-HN3 lightly, then LI4 and GB20 for 30–60 s. You can do the session 1–2 times a day during the pollen season.
Apasă ușor-mediu 30–60 s pe fiecare punc: Press lightly to moderately for 30–60 s on each point, in small circles, on the affected shoulder. Alternate with slow movements, within comfort, 1–2 times a day.
Apasă ușor-mediu 30–60 s pe punctele de: Press lightly to moderately for 30–60 s on the wrist points, with no pressure on the numb area. Place the wrist in a neutral position and repeat 1–2 times a day.

Ce NU poate face? Nu poate stabili boli,: What can it NOT do? It cannot establish diseases, it cannot rule out serious conditions on the basis of the pulse or tongue, and it cannot decide on its own to stop or replace a treatment. It cannot interpret someone else’s pulse to “tell them what they have.” A coated tongue or a “tense” pulse neither confirms nor rules out any disease. Anyone who claims otherwise goes beyond what the evidence can support.

Cefalee de tensiune: tensiunea din ceafă: Tension headache: tension in the neck and shoulders often sustains the pain. Start with GB20, in the hollows at the base of the skull, pressing with your thumbs and letting your head rest gently backward. Continue with LI4 and the temples (EX-HN5), then the area between the eyebrows (EX-HN3), using small, slow touches. TCM rationale: GB20 “releases wind” from the head; modern rationale: relaxation of the suboccipital muscles and distraction from the pain.

Cele opt principii (Ba Gang) sunt un cad: The eight principles (Ba Gang) are a framework for classifying a patient’s picture into four pairs of opposites: Yin–Yang (the general category), Exterior–Interior (depth of the disease), Cold–Heat (nature of the process) and Full (excess)–Empty (deficiency), which describes the relationship between the strength of the pathogenic factor and the body’s resistance. For example, pain that worsens with cold and eases with warmth would be interpreted as a “Cold” pattern; restlessness with thirst and a red face as a “Heat” pattern.

They are used in pairs, for example SP4 with PC6 or LU7 with KI6.

When you see “Stomach Meridian,” think of a network of points along the traditional pathway, not a channel that would lead to the anatomical stomach. This distinction protects you from two errors: rejecting everything without understanding, and taking everything literally.

Distinguishing between “this is what the tradition says” and “this is what the evidence shows” remains the golden rule.

Diagnosticul în MTC se bazează pe patru: Diagnosis in TCM rests on four methods (Si Zhen), used together. Inspection (Wang) looks at the general appearance, facial color, state of the spirit, posture and above all the tongue: color, shape, coating. Auscultation and olfaction (Wen) means listening to the voice, breathing and cough, as well as noting odors. Inquiry (Wen, with a different tone in Chinese) is a detailed interview: pain, cold or heat, sweating, appetite, sleep, stool, urine, menstrual cycle, emotions. Palpation (Qie) includes taking the pulse at the wrist and palpating painful areas or points.

Dien Chan este o metodă vietnameză creat: Dien Chan is a Vietnamese method created by Bui Quoc Chau in the 1980s, which uses the face as a reflex map, with sticks and rollers. The tradition holds that there are correspondences between facial points and organs, but this system is recent, has no documented classical roots, and quality clinical studies are, as far as we know, absent or very few.
Diferența esențială: Zang-Fu sunt sistem: The essential difference: Zang-Fu are functional systems, not anatomical organs in the Western sense. The TCM “Spleen” is linked to digestion, the transformation of food and the maintenance of fluids, rather than to the lymphoid organ we know from anatomy. The “Kidney” encompasses aspects of growth, reproduction, bones and water. That is why the statement “the Spleen is weak” in TCM does not mean the organ is diseased in a medical analysis.

Dovezile pentru acupresura în amețeală s: The evidence for acupressure in dizziness is weak; the cause must be medically evaluated before any comfort measure.
Dovezile pentru acupresura în extremităț: The evidence for acupressure in cold extremities is weak; massage may temporarily increase the sensation of warmth through local circulation.
Dovezile pentru acupresura în nicturie s: The evidence for acupressure in nocturia is weak; investigating the cause is essential.
Dovezile pentru acupresura în somnul înt: The evidence for acupressure in interrupted sleep comes from small studies; the likely effect is relaxation. Sleep hygiene and evaluation of causes are essential.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură sau acupresu: The evidence for acupuncture or acupressure in primary hyperhidrosis is weak; the effect, if any, is probably relaxation.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în acnee sun: The evidence for acupuncture in acne is weak; acupressure alone has no evidence, and dermatological treatment remains the mainstay.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în astm sunt: The evidence for acupuncture in asthma is weak and inconsistent; guidelines do not recommend it as a treatment. At most it can be a relaxation adjuvant.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în ciclurile: The evidence for acupuncture in irregular cycles (for example polycystic ovary syndrome) is weak and of low quality; acupressure is a relaxation adjuvant.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în colonul i: The evidence for acupuncture in irritable bowel is limited and inconsistent; acupressure and relaxation may reduce the stress associated with symptoms, as an adjuvant.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în durerea d: The evidence for acupuncture in elbow pain is limited and of modest quality; acupressure may offer short-term comfort, as an adjuvant to exercise.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în fasciita: The evidence for acupuncture in plantar fasciitis is limited; acupressure and massage of the sole may improve comfort, as an adjuvant to stretching.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în prevenire: The evidence for acupuncture in preventing recurrent cystitis is limited, from small studies; it does not replace prophylaxis and medical treatment.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură în sinuzita: The evidence for acupuncture in chronic sinusitis is limited; acupressure may ease the sensation of pressure, without treating the infection.
Dovezile pentru acupunctură/acupresură î: The evidence for acupuncture/acupressure in PMS is limited, from small studies; it may ease some comfort symptoms, but it is not a proven treatment.
The evidence for acupuncture/acupressure in chronic constipation is limited and heterogeneous; abdominal self-massage may help comfort, alongside fiber and hydration.
The evidence for acupuncture/acupressure in enuresis is weak; behavioral approaches and the enuresis alarm have better evidence.
The evidence for acupuncture/acupressure in reflux is weak; lifestyle measures and medical treatment remain the mainstay.
The evidence for acupuncture/acupressure in panic disorder is weak; the mainstay treatments are psychotherapy and, if needed, medication.
Dovezile sunt în general de calitate scă: The evidence is generally of low quality, with studies that are hard to link to a sham control.

: Sprijină ceafa în mâini și apasă sub c: : Cradle the nape in your hands and press upward under the skull, then knead the shoulders.

Alege ulei sau loțiune simple, fără parf: Choose a simple, unscented oil or lotion, such as plain food-grade vegetable oil (for example olive or sunflower; almond oil only if you are not allergic to nuts) or unscented lotion.

Alunecă cu palma întreagă, relaxată, pe: Glide with the whole relaxed palm on the skin, in a long, slow movement, usually from the extremity toward the trunk. The hand stays soft and molds to the shape; the rhythm is steady, like calm breathing. A thin layer of oil or lotion helps the glide.

Așază arătătorul, mijlociul și inelarul: Place the index, middle and ring fingers of one hand in front of the ear, from top to bottom: TE21, SI19 and GB2, in the hollows you feel when you open your mouth. Press slowly with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10) forward, keeping your mouth slightly open, then repeat on the other side.
Așază degetele mari la capătul dinspre n: Place your thumbs at the nose end of the eyebrow, in the notch of the bone (BL2), on the bone, not behind it, and press gently upward, toward the forehead, without pushing toward the eye. With the tips of your index fingers, at the same time, press on the brow bone, level with EX-HN4, at the middle of the eyebrow. Never press on the eyeball.
Așază o minge de tenis între spate și pe: Place a tennis ball between your back and the wall, to the side of the spine, and make small knee bends to roll it over the muscle. Stay 20–30 s on tender spots, without sharp pain. The ball must not touch the spine or bone directly.
Așază podul palmei sau partea cărnoasă a: Place the heel of your palm or the fleshy part of your forearm on the muscle and let your body weight provide the pressure, not the strength of your arm. Slide slowly or stay still for 10–20 s. Keep asking your partner how it feels.
Așază vârfurile arătătoarelor în șanțuri: Place the tips of your index fingers in the grooves next to the wings of the nose, on both LI20, and press gently toward the bone, upward and inward, for 20–30 seconds, then gently in small circles. Then, separately, press with your middle finger between the eyebrows (Yintang) for 15–20 seconds.
BL60 se omite în sarcină. Fără presiune: BL60 is omitted in pregnancy. No strong pressure if you have edema, varicose veins or skin lesions at the ankle.

Coloana vertebrală, zona rinichilor, abd: Spine, kidney area, abdomen, neck, bones; generally deep pressure.
Coloană, rinichi (zona lombară laterală): Spine, kidneys (lateral lumbar area), head, neck, abdomen, bones, joints, areas with varicose veins or bruises; severe osteoporosis.
Coloană, zona rinichilor, gât, osteoporo: Spine, kidney area, neck, severe osteoporosis, varicose veins or thrombosis; if numbness or pain running down the leg appears, stop.
Cu degetul mijlociu al unei mâini apasă: With the middle finger of one hand, press rhythmically on GV20, at the crown of the head, and with the middle finger of the other hand press on Taiyang, on one side, with presses of 2–3 seconds. Breathe deeply and alertly for 30–45 seconds, then switch temples.
Cu febră sau stare generală alterată, am: With a fever or poor general condition, postpone the massage until you have recovered.
Cu limfedem sau după îndepărtarea gangli: With lymphedema or after removal of lymph nodes, do not massage the limb without your doctor's approval.
Cu mâna opusă prinde antebrațul: degetul: With the opposite hand, grasp the forearm: thumb on LI10, 2 cun below the elbow crease, on the muscle, and the tip of the middle finger on LI11, at the outer end of the crease of the bent elbow. Press both at once, gently and deeply, then slightly extend and bend the arm.
Cu mâna opusă prinde umărul: vârful arăt: With the opposite hand, grasp the shoulder: tip of the index finger in the hollow in front of the acromion (LI15), and tip of the thumb in the hollow behind it (TE14), like a pincer. Press both at once, gently and deeply, then make small slow movements of the arm if you feel comfortable.
Cu mâna opusă pune degetul mare pe LI4,: With the opposite hand, place your thumb on LI4, in the muscle between the thumb and index finger, and the tip of your index finger on SI3, on the ulnar edge of the hand, behind the joint of the little finger, when the fist is slightly clenched. If you cannot reach both points at once, press them in turn, 20–30 seconds each, with comfortable medium pressure, then switch hands.
Cu mâna opusă pune degetul mare pe PC6 p: With the opposite hand, place your thumb on PC6 on the palm side and your index finger on TE5, exactly opposite, on the back of the forearm. Squeeze gently, like a pincer, keeping the pressure constant and breathing slowly.
Cu mâna relaxată, lovește rapid și ușor: With a relaxed hand, tap quickly and lightly with the edge of the hand (the little-finger side) or with a cupped hand, alternating hands. The movement comes from the wrist, not the shoulder, and the taps are springy, not heavy. If a tap feels “in the bone,” stop and move your hand to a thicker muscle.
Cu o mână pune degetul mare pe KI3, în a: With one hand, place your thumb on KI3, in the hollow between the inner ankle bone and the Achilles tendon, and your index finger on BL60, exactly opposite, between the outer ankle bone and the tendon. Squeeze gently like a pincer for 60 seconds, then switch feet.
Cu o mână pune degetul mare pe LR3, pe d: With one hand, place your thumb on LR3, on the top of the foot, in the hollow where the metatarsal bones of toes 1 and 2 meet. With the other hand, press with your thumb on SP4, in the arch of the foot, on the inner edge. Press both at once, with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10), for 60 seconds.
Cu pulpa degetului mare sau a arătătorul: With the pad of your thumb or index finger, press lightly to moderately (3–5/10) and make small circles; on the temples, only gently, 1–2 cm, moving the skin along with your finger. Keep a slow rhythm, about one circle per second. Change direction after 30 s if it is comfortable.
Cu tromboză venoasă profundă cunoscută s: If you have known or suspected deep vein thrombosis (swollen, painful, warm, red calf), do not massage the area and seek urgent medical attention.
Cu un deget mare pe KI1, în talpă la uni: With one thumb on KI1, on the sole where the front third meets the middle third, and with the other thumb on KI3, in the hollow between the inner ankle bone and the Achilles tendon, press both at the same time with medium, comfortable pressure (4–6/10). Breathe slowly for 60–90 seconds, then switch feet.
Cu vârfurile a două degete ale unei mâin: With the fingertips of two fingers of one hand, press lightly on LU1, below the collarbone, level with the shoulder, and with the palm of the other hand touch CV17, on the breastbone, between the nipples, with very light pressure. Take deep breaths for 45–60 seconds, then switch sides.

Dacă ai boli de inimă, hipertensiune gre: If you have heart disease, hard-to-control high blood pressure or rhythm disorders, ask your doctor first.
Dacă ai cancer, în curs de chimioterapie: If you have cancer, are undergoing chemotherapy or radiotherapy, or have recently finished treatment, get the approval of your medical team.
Dacă ai diabet cu neuropatie sau sensibi: If you have diabetes with neuropathy or reduced sensation in the foot, wounds, fungal infections, blisters or heel pain, do not do this exercise without your doctor's approval.
Dacă ai diabet, mai ales cu neuropatie s: If you have diabetes, especially with neuropathy or reduced sensation in the feet, talk to your doctor before foot massage.
Dacă ai durere în piept, dificultăți de: If you have chest pain, difficulty breathing, sudden weakness, speech difficulties or heavy bleeding, call 112. Do not use acupressure instead of medical help.
Dacă ai osteoporoză, hernie de disc, dur: If you have osteoporosis, a herniated disc, radicular pain or spinal conditions, get your doctor's approval.
Dacă durerea este nouă, intensă, nu se a: If the pain is new, intense, does not improve within a few days or appears after an injury, you need a medical consultation, not massage.
Dacă nu bifezi nimic, aplicația nu poate: If you tick nothing, the app cannot know what is unsuitable for you. When you have an illness or take a treatment, ask your doctor before massage or acupressure.
Dacă partenerul spune „oprește”, te opre: If the partner says "stop", you stop immediately, no discussion.

Deplasează încet un membru până când sim: Slowly move a limb until you feel a light, pleasant stretch, then stay there. Breathe slowly; on the exhale, the partner or you may increase the angle very slightly, only if it stays comfortable. Do not force it, do not bounce, do not go to the point of pain.
Destinderea mușchilor din ceafă și umeri: Relaxing the neck and shoulder muscles in a gentle massage between two partners.
Destinderea mâinilor și antebrațelor dup: Relaxing the hands and forearms after work at the keyboard and mouse.
După fracturi sau operații recente nu ma: After recent fractures or surgery, do not massage the area (typically until medical clearance) and do not force the joints to move.
După masaj bea apă și odihnește-te câtev: After the massage, drink water and rest for a few minutes before getting up suddenly.
Durere ascuțită, arsură sau junghi în ti: Sharp pain, burning or stabbing pain during the massage.
Durere care coboară în braț, amorțeală,: Pain that radiates down the arm, numbness, dizziness, a recent neck injury or an acute cervical disc herniation.
Durere care coboară în picior, slăbiciun: Pain that radiates down the leg, weakness or numbness, fever, a recent injury, lumbar surgery; not on the kidneys and not directly on the spine.
Durere care se agravează în orele sau în: Pain that gets worse in the hours or the day after, compared with before the massage.
Durere cervicală: efecte mici, încredere: Neck pain: small effects, limited confidence
Durere după operație: reducere raportată: Pain after surgery: reduction reported, but studies differ widely
Durere lombară cronică: dovezile pentru: Chronic low back pain: the evidence for massage is weak
Durerea ascuțită, arsura sau furnicături: Sharp pain, burning or tingling may indicate a nerve or joint problem. Avoid pressure on the area and seek a medical consultation.
Durerea persistentă sau care revine meri: Persistent or recurring pain deserves a doctor's evaluation. The routines below are for comfort only.
Dureri puternice, amorțeală în brațe, am: Severe pain, numbness in the arms, dizziness, a recent neck injury, acute cervical disc herniation; no pressure on the side of the neck.
Energie dimineața: creștet și tâmplă: Morning energy: crown of the head and temple
Evită presiunea puternică pe capul fibul: Avoid strong pressure on the head of the fibula (peroneal nerve). No pressure in case of varicose veins or thrombosis.
Evită punctele la care cardul afișează „: Avoid the points for which the card shows "Avoid in pregnancy" (for example LI4, SP6, GB21, BL60, ST25, CV4, CV6, CV12, BL32), as well as LR3, SP4, KI3 (ankle) and the lumbosacral points (BL25, BL26, GB30), and any firm pressure on the legs.
Evită uleiurile din nuci sau arahide dac: Avoid nut or peanut oils if you or the partner have food allergies, and undiluted concentrated essential oils on the skin.
Febră peste 38 °C sau stare generală alt: Fever above 38 °C or a poor general condition
Febră, sarcină (omite pasul cu abdomenul: Fever, pregnancy (skip the abdomen step), right after a meal, wounds, severe varicose veins, thrombosis.
Fii blând și evită presiunea intensă. În: Be gentle and avoid intense pressure. In pregnancy skip LI4 (step 6) and ask for your doctor's approval.
Folosește doar presiune ușoară spre medi: Use only light to medium pressure, long strokes and gentle kneading on the back and shoulders, with your doctor's approval; do not knead or press the calves (higher risk of thrombosis in pregnancy).
Furnicături, amorțeală sau slăbiciune ca: Tingling, numbness or weakness that appears or persists after you lower your hand.
Fă fiecare pas fără grabă; dacă timpul e: Take each step without rushing; if time is short, skip the abdomen or leg steps. During pregnancy, skip the steps on the abdomen (CV12, ST25), the lumbar area (BL25, BL26), the ankle and foot (SP6, LR3) and the points LI4, GB21; ask your doctor for approval. Stop the sequence if you feel sharp pain, numbness or dizziness.
Fă secvența pe ambele mâini. Furnicături: Do the sequence on both hands. Tingling or numbness in the fingers: stop and seek medical advice. During pregnancy, omit LI4 (step 5) and ask your doctor for approval.
Fă secvența pe ambele picioare. Presiune: Do the sequence on both feet. Pressure of 4–6 out of 10. During pregnancy, omit the points on the ankle and foot (KI3, BL60, LR3) and firm pressure on the legs; ask your doctor for approval.
Fă un test pe piele: pune o picătură pe: Do a skin test: put a drop on the inside of your forearm, wait 24 hours and watch for redness or itching.
Fără presiune directă pe coloană. BL23 ș: No direct pressure on the spine. BL23 and BL52 are at the level of the kidneys: omit them if you have kidney disease or kidney stones. Lower back pain with numbness, fever or after an injury: seek medical attention. During pregnancy, gentle pressure only, avoiding the sacral area.
Fără presiune în caz de răni, varice, ed: No pressure in case of wounds, varicose veins, edema or diabetic neuropathy of the foot. Do not press KI3 strongly.
GB21 se omite în sarcină, fiind tradițio: GB21 is omitted during pregnancy, as it is traditionally contraindicated. The pressure should not radiate into the arm like an electric current; if you feel it, reduce or stop.
GB21 se omite în sarcină. Nu apăsa pe pa: GB21 is omitted during pregnancy. Do not press on the side of the neck. If you have pain that runs down the arm or numbness, stop and seek medical advice.
Genunchi și gambă: ST36 și SP: Knee and calf: ST36 and SP
Genunchi și gambă: ST36 și SP6: Knee and calf: ST36 and SP6
Ghidul NICE NG59 spune că poate fi luată: The NICE NG59 guideline states that manual therapy, including soft-tissue techniques such as massage, may be considered only as part of a treatment package that includes physical exercise, with or without psychological therapy. O meta-analiză din 2022 (33 de studii ra: A 2022 meta-analysis (33 randomized trials) reported reduced postoperative pain after massage, but heterogeneity was extremely high, no trial was double-blind, and the real effect is uncertain. Massage after surgery is done only with the agreement of the medical team.
O meta-analiză din 2024 a 39 de studii r: A 2024 meta-analysis of 39 randomized trials on acupressure (3,395 participants) reported reduced anxiety, but heterogeneity was very high (up to 100%), almost all trials had a risk of bias, and in comparisons with sham (placebo) acupressure the difference was not statistically significant. The authors acknowledge the low quality of the studies. The results suggest a possible relaxation effect, not firm evidence, and do not replace treatment for persistent anxiety.

Partenerul apasă cu degetele mari pe amb: The partner presses with both thumbs on both LR3, on the top of the foot, in the hollow where the bones of toes 1 and 2 meet. At the same time, you press LI4 on one hand with the thumb of the other, for 30 seconds, then switch hands for another 30 seconds (LR3 stay pressed the whole time). Before you begin, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 4–6 out of 10); the person being pressed can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.
Partenerul prinde occiputul cu o mână, c: The partner holds the occiput with one hand, with the thumb and middle finger on the two GB20, in a pincer across the nape. With the thumb of the other hand they press gently into the central hollow, GV16, below the occipital protuberance, upward and slightly forward. Pressure stays light to moderate (3–5/10). Before you begin, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 3–5 out of 10); the person being pressed can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.
Partenerul pune degetul mare pe GB21, pe: The partner places a thumb on GB21, on the trapezius muscle, halfway between the nape and the tip of the shoulder, and presses slowly downward, into the muscle, without pushing deep toward the lung apex. With the thumb of the other hand they press simultaneously on SI11, in the hollow below the middle of the scapular spine, on the muscle (not with the elbow). You tell them when the pressure reaches 4–6/10 and breathe slowly. Before you begin, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 4–6 out of 10); the person being pressed can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.
Partenerul pune degetul mare pe LI11, la: The partner places a thumb on LI11, at the end of the elbow crease, and the other thumb on LI4, in the muscle between the thumb and index finger. They press simultaneously with medium pressure, hold 45–60 seconds while you breathe slowly, then switch arms. Before you begin, agree on a stop signal (“stop” or a raised hand). The person pressing asks “how is the pressure?” at the start and every 15–20 seconds (target: 4–6 out of 10); the person being pressed can ask for lighter, firmer or stopping at any time, without explanation.

Prinde ceafa în cupă, cu degetele împreu: Cup the back of the neck with your fingers interlaced beneath it, and place your thumbs on both GB20, in the hollows below the occiput. Prinde lobul între degetul mare și arătă: Grasp the lobe between thumb and index finger and gently massage it in small circles. Continue along the edge of the ear, upward, with slow movements. Then you may gently pull the ear sideways and downward a few times, without pain.
Prinde mușchiul între degetul mare și re: Grasp the muscle between your thumb and the rest of your fingers, lift it slightly and squeeze it gently, then let go, as if kneading soft dough. Move your hands slowly, with a rhythmic motion. If sharp pain occurs, reduce the pressure immediately.
Prinde un pliu de piele între degetele m: Grasp a fold of skin between your thumbs and the other fingers and "roll" it forward, like a wave, moving your thumbs forward. If the skin does not lift easily or it hurts a lot, give up on that area. The movement is slow and without pinching.
Prinde ușor mâna, antebrațul sau gamba ș: Gently hold the hand, forearm or calf and shake quickly with a small amplitude, as if shaking a rope. The muscles stay relaxed, with no jerking and no strong pulling on the joint. Finish with a few slow strokes.

Un review Cochrane despre masaj, cu sau: A Cochrane review on massage, with or without aromatherapy, in people with cancer rated most outcomes as very low certainty; only one outcome (medium-term anxiety, aromatherapy with massage) was rated moderate. Massage can be a support for relaxation, not a treatment for the disease, and should be discussed with the oncology team.
Un review Cochrane din 2015 (25 de studi: A 2015 Cochrane review (25 studies, 3,096 participants) rated the evidence as low or very low quality. Massage reduced pain in the short term compared with no treatment, but not in the long term, and the authors said they have “very little confidence” that massage is effective. No serious adverse events were reported; most often, pain increased temporarily.
Un rezumat de congres (World Physiothera: A conference abstract (World Physiotherapy) on the update of a Cochrane review (44 studies) concluded that the studies are of low quality and that no firm recommendation can be made for or against massage. Small to medium effects appeared mainly after large, repeated doses of massage; the reported side effects were minor and transient, such as local tenderness.

În sarcină cere sfatul medicului înainte: In pregnancy, ask the doctor for advice before PC6. If you have carpal tunnel syndrome, reduce the pressure. Chest pain, strong palpitations or fainting: stop and call 112.
În sarcină cere sfatul medicului. Greața: In pregnancy, ask the doctor for advice. Nausea with chest pain or pressure, sweating, shortness of breath, severe headache, intense dizziness, weakness or slurred speech: call 112. Repeated vomiting, fever, strong abdominal pain, signs of dehydration (dry mouth, little urine) or vomiting during pregnancy: medical consultation the same day. During chemotherapy, talk to the oncology team.
În sarcină nu masa tălpile, gleznele și: In pregnancy, do not massage the soles, ankles and hand (LI4, SP6, BL60, LR3, SP4, KI3) unless the doctor or midwife approves. With diabetes and reduced sensation in the foot, only with the doctor's approval.
În sarcină omite CV3–CV7 și orice presiu: In pregnancy, skip CV3–CV7 and any pressure on the abdomen. No pressure with abdominal or inguinal hernia, heavy menstruation, abdominal inflammation or acute pain.
În sarcină omite complet CV12 și ST25 (z: In pregnancy, skip CV12 and ST25 completely (abdominal area). No pressure with abdominal or inguinal hernia, active ulcer, abdominal inflammation, recent procedures, cirrhosis or fluid in the abdomen, known abdominal aortic aneurysm, stoma or pump, heavy menstruation or acute abdominal pain (especially lower right, with fever or vomiting: possible appendicitis, do not press and see a doctor). Do not begin if you have repeated vomiting, a swollen and hard abdomen, you are not passing gas or stool, you see blood in the stool or vomit, you have flank pain with fever, or your period is late and pregnancy has not been ruled out.
În sarcină: prudență. Evită acest punct: In pregnancy: caution. Avoid this point or ask the doctor or midwife for approval.

După 1950, în China s-a produs o standar: After 1950, standardization took place in China: unified textbooks, state schools, integration into hospitals. The World Health Organization later published the standard point nomenclature, the one we use in the app (for example LI4, ST36). In 2010, UNESCO inscribed "Acupuncture and moxibustion of traditional Chinese medicine" on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

Limita cea mai importantă este diagnosti: The most important limit is diagnosis. Self-treatment with points may ease a discomfort, but it does not replace medical evaluation. A new, intense or persistent symptom may be the sign of a problem that needs specific treatment. Do not delay a consultation because of a "natural" method and do not stop prescribed treatment without your physician's approval.
Limitate pentru majoritatea indicațiilor: Limited for most indications; for breech presentation, a Cochrane review shows fewer non-cephalic presentations at birth with moxibustion plus usual care (moderate certainty), with no clear difference in the cesarean rate.
Limitate și de calitate scăzută; hărțile: Limited and of low quality; ear point maps are not supported by solid evidence, and part of the effect may be contextual.
Limitate: posibilă ameliorare a durerii: Limited: possible short-term pain relief (e.g. chronic low back pain, studies of low methodological quality); long-term effects are unclear, and some syntheses show no advantage over placebo.
Limitate; calitatea studiilor este scăzu: Limited; study quality is low and the mechanism is not clearly established; some studies for neck and low back pain.
Limitate; efect probabil prin mișcare și: Limited; effect probably through movement and breathing.
Limitate; meta-analize mici indică ameli: Limited; small meta-analyses indicate improvement in musculoskeletal pain, but the studies are mostly small and of low quality.
Limitate; o meta-analiză din 2022 arată: Limited; a 2022 meta-analysis shows an increase in pressure pain threshold, but not a decrease in patient-reported pain; small studies.
Limitate; o sinteză din 2025 raportează: Limited; a 2025 review reports pain reduction with low to moderate certainty, but with very high heterogeneity, small samples, risk of bias and publication bias; parameters (wavelength, power, dose) are inconsistently reported.
Limitate; o sinteză sistematică (6 studi: Limited; a systematic review (6 trials, follow-up 7–21 days) suggests short-term effects on musculoskeletal pain, especially spinal; small studies.
Limitate; pentru TENS în durerea cronică: Limited; for TENS in chronic pain, a Cochrane overview shows very low certainty; for TEAS in postoperative nausea and vomiting, recent reviews report benefits as an adjunct to antiemetics, but the studies are heterogeneous, mostly from China, with difficult blinding.
Limitate; studii clinice de calitate puț: Limited; few quality clinical trials, the "specific spectrum" mechanism is not demonstrated.
Limitate; studii mici sugerează ameliora: Limited; small studies suggest temporary pain relief and relaxation, but practitioners' claims often exceed what has been clinically demonstrated.
Limitate; unele componente (auriculo) cu: Limited; some components (auriculo) have mixed evidence.
Limitate; unele rezultate pozitive în re: Limited; some positive results in rehabilitation, but low quality.
Limitate; unele sinteze arată beneficii: Limited; some reviews show benefits (e.g. knee osteoarthritis, postoperative nausea), but study quality is variable and results versus sham are inconsistent.
Limitate; unele studii mici arată reduce: Limited; some small studies show short-term pain reduction.
Limitate; unele studii pentru dureri art: Limited; some studies for joint pain and digestion.
Limitate–moderate pentru anxietate, depr: Limited to moderate for anxiety, depression, PTSD in meta-analyses (many authors are practitioners; comparisons with standard therapies are few); the specific role of the points is disputed.

MTC împarte tradițional cauzele bolii în: TCM traditionally divides the causes of disease into three major categories. The external causes are six climatic influences called "perverse energies": Wind, Cold, Summer-Heat, Dampness, Dryness and Fire. The internal causes are the seven emotions (joy, anger, worry, overthinking, sadness, fear, fright) when they are excessive or prolonged. The third category, the neutral causes, includes disordered diet, overwork, lack of exercise, excesses, trauma and exhaustion.

Marma de pe picior (Kshipra), mână (Tala: Marma of the foot (Kshipra), hand (Talahridaya), head and neck
Marma provine din Ayurveda; marmele sunt: Marma comes from Ayurveda; marmas are vital points, associated with anatomical structures (joints, vessels, nerves), considered in tradition to be points where "Prana" accumulates. Marma therapy uses gentle pressure, sometimes with oils. Tradition speaks of 107 marmas; similarities with acupuncture appear here, but the theory is different. What they have in common: all work with pressure, have an energetic theory and are, in practice, forms of therapeutic massage. What differs: the conception of the body, the physical style and the training of practitioners. Research on them is limited and of variable quality; there is modest evidence for reduced pain and tension with massage and soft manipulation, but not for the energetic theory. Treat them as comfort care, with the same precautions as in acupressure.
Marma sunt zone vitale descrise în Sushr: Marma are vital areas described in the Sushruta Samhita and in Kalaripayattu.
Marma: puncte vitale ayurvedice, presiun: Marma: Ayurvedic vital points, gentle pressure, a theory different from TCM.
Masaj abdominal blând în sens orar, 60–9: Gentle clockwise abdominal massage, 60–90 s, then light to medium pressure on ST36, LR3 and SP4, 30–60 s. Practice daily, in the evening, in a relaxed state.
Masaj abdominal foarte blând în sens ora: Very gentle clockwise abdominal massage, 20–30 s, as a relaxing game, with a warm hand; no pressure on points in small children. Stop if the child cries or feels pain.
Masaj blând al abdomenului inferior și p: Gentle massage of the lower abdomen and medium pressure for 30–60 s on the other points, in the second half of the day, as a relaxation technique. Do not use to "induce" menstruation.
Masaj blând al gambelor și coapselor, 20: Gentle massage of the calves and thighs, 20–30 s, with a warm hand, as a moment of closeness; no pressure on points. Stop if there is pain on touch.
Masaj blând al mâinilor și tălpilor, apo: Gentle massage of the hands and soles, then medium pressure for 30–60 s on the indicated points. You can combine it with a warm shower or warm compresses. In pregnancy omit LI4.
Masaj circular blând în sensul acelor de: Gentle clockwise circular massage around the navel, 60–90 s, then press ST36 and SP4 for 30–60 s. Do not press hard on a full abdomen.
Masaj foarte ușor al palmelor, tălpilor: Very light massage of the palms, soles and forehead, 20–30 s, in an evening ritual; do not press points. Add warmth and a calm voice.
Chinese therapeutic massage, part of TCM.
Masaj tradițional pe linii, cu frământar: Traditional massage along lines, with kneading and gentle pressure; a precursor of shiatsu. In Japan it was traditionally a profession of blind people.
Masajul și acupresura se suprapun; alege: Massage and acupressure overlap; the choice depends on preference and tolerance.
Masează cu degetele cercuri mici în fața: Massage small circles with your fingers in front of the ear and on the masseter muscle, 30–60 s, with light to medium pressure and a relaxed jaw. Repeat in the evening and morning.
Masează cu degetele mari, 30–60 s pe pun: Massage with your thumbs, 30–60 s per point, with medium pressure and slow breathing; avoid strong pressure on the sides and front of the neck, where the arteries pass. You can do the session 1–2 times a day, combined with slow head tilts.
Masează cu mișcări circulare, în sensul: Massage in circular, clockwise movements around the navel (ST25) for 60–90 s, then gently press LI4, LI11 and ST36 for 30–60 s. Do it in the morning, 20–30 min after a meal.
Masează ușor CV12 cu cercuri mici, 60 s,: Gently massage CV12 with small circles, 60 s, then ST36, PC6 and the other points, 30–60 s, with slow breathing. Do it 1–2 hours after a meal, not immediately.
Masează ușor CV12 și apasă PC6, ST36 și: Gently massage CV12 and press PC6, ST36 and LR3 for 30–60 s, away from mealtimes (not immediately after). The pressure should be gentle, not on a full stomach.
Masează ușor CV17 (mijlocul pieptului) 3: Gently massage CV17 (middle of the chest) for 30–60 s, then press LU7, LU9 and BL13/EX-B1 (on the back, if someone can reach). Gentle pressure, once or twice a day.
Masează ușor LI20 (lângă nări) și EX-HN3: Gently massage LI20 (beside the nostrils) and EX-HN3 for 30–60 s, then LU7, GB20 and LI4. You can do the session 2–3 times a day while you have symptoms.
Masează ușor în jurul ombilicului și apa: Gently massage around the navel and press ST36 and SP9 softly, 30–60 s, once or twice. Gentle warmth on the abdomen may help; the pressure should not be painful.
Masează încet baza craniului (GB20) cu d: Slowly massage the base of the skull (GB20) with your thumbs, then the temples and the spot between the eyebrows, 30–60 s per point. Repeat as needed, up to 3 times a day.
Masează-ți 2 minute talpa cu degetele ma: Massage your sole for 2 minutes with your thumbs, with soft pressure, around the KI1 area (roughly where the front and middle thirds of the sole meet), breathing slowly. The goal is relaxation; do not look for "correspondences with organs". Avoid if you have wounds, infections or thrombosis in the leg.

Menținerea la 2–3 cm de punct: Holding at 2–3 cm from the point
Menținerea presiunii fixe sau cu cercuri: Holding steady pressure or small circles for 30–90 s
Mergi la dermatolog dacă acneea este sev: See a dermatologist if the acne is severe, painful cysts or scars appear, it affects self-esteem, it appears suddenly in adulthood with other symptoms (hirsutism, irregular cycles) or after new medications.
Mergi la medic dacă ai durere severă dup: See a doctor if you have severe pain after a blow, cannot put weight on the foot, have marked swelling, redness and warmth or fever, or the pain persists beyond a few months despite measures.
Mergi la medic dacă ai infecții foarte f: See a doctor if you have very frequent or severe infections, recurrent fever, unexplained weight loss, night sweats, enlarged lymph nodes, unusual infections or delayed healing.
Mergi la medic dacă ai: febră mare, dure: See a doctor if you have: high fever, pain or swelling around the eye, vision disturbances, severe headache or stiff neck, symptoms lasting more than 10 days without improvement, persistent purulent discharge.
Mergi la medic dacă ai: sforăit puternic: See a doctor if you have: loud snoring with breathing pauses, waking up gasping, frequent nighttime urination, nighttime pain, dangerous daytime sleepiness, depressive symptoms.
Mergi la medic dacă ai: slăbiciune sau p: See a doctor if you have: weakness or loss of grip strength, atrophy of the muscles at the base of the thumb, permanent numbness, symptoms after trauma, bilateral symptoms with swelling or other general signs. Left untreated for a long time, the nerve can be permanently damaged. In pregnancy omit LI4.
Mergi la medic dacă ai: sânge în urină,: See a doctor if you have: blood in the urine, pain, fever, inability to urinate, new discharge, neurological symptoms, frequent urination with great thirst (possible diabetes).
Mergi la medic dacă ai: umflătură marcat: See a doctor if you have: marked swelling, deformity after trauma, fever, redness and warmth at the elbow, numbness or weakness of the hand, intense nighttime pain or pain that does not improve within a few weeks.
Mergi la medic dacă copilul are: durere: See a doctor if the child has: severe abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in the stool, a swollen abdomen, fever, weight loss, constipation since birth, constipation lasting more than 2 weeks, or soiling of clothes.
Mergi la medic dacă copilul sforăie pute: See a doctor if the child snores loudly with breathing pauses, has frequent nightmares or night terrors, daytime sleepiness, learning/behavior difficulties, or if insomnia lasts more than 4 weeks.
Mergi la medic dacă degetele devin alb–a: See a doctor if the fingers turn white–blue–red (Raynaud), ulcers appear, there is intense pain, black or numb skin, known circulation disorders or diabetes, or if the coldness is new and accompanied by fatigue, weight gain or dizziness.
Mergi la medic dacă durerea este unilate: See a doctor if the pain is one-sided, constant, occurs during the day, with limping, swelling, redness, fever, weight loss, marked fatigue, bone or joint pain, or often wakes the child.
Mergi la medic dacă insomnia durează pes: See a doctor if insomnia lasts more than 3 months, loud snoring with breathing pauses occurs, dangerous daytime sleepiness, very low mood, thoughts of harming yourself, or if you use alcohol/sleeping pills.
Mergi la medic dacă nicturia este nouă s: See a doctor if nocturia is new or frequent (>2 per night), with great thirst (diabetes), leg swelling, difficulty breathing, weak urine stream (prostate), blood in the urine, fever or pain.
Mergi la medic dacă oboseala persistă pe: See a doctor if fatigue persists beyond 2–4 weeks, occurs with weight loss, fever, bleeding, difficulty breathing, palpitations, very low mood, or dangerous sleepiness while driving.
Mergi la medic dacă pielea este infectat: See a doctor if the skin is infected (pus, yellow crust, fever), the eczema spreads quickly, sleep is affected, it appears in an infant, it does not respond to treatment, or painful blisters appear.
Mergi la medic dacă simptomele afectează: See a doctor if the symptoms affect work and relationships, you have very low mood or thoughts of harming yourself (112), unusual bleeding, new pelvic pain, or symptoms that continue after menstruation.
Mergi urgent la medic (sau sună la 112): See a doctor urgently (or call 112) for: chest pain or difficulty breathing, sudden weakness of one part of the body, violent headache, "the worst of your life", high fever with neck stiffness, unexplained bleeding, weight loss for no reason, severe abdominal pain, symptoms in pregnancy or in small children. Always tell your doctor which complementary methods you use.
Mergi urgent la medic dacă apar: scădere: See a doctor urgently if the following occur: sudden loss of vision, severe eye pain, halos around lights, a painful red eye, trauma, double vision, new floaters or a "curtain" in the visual field.
Mergi urgent la medic/112 dacă copilul a: See a doctor urgently/call 112 if the child has: rapid or labored breathing, chest retractions, bluish lips, fever (any fever under 3 months), refusal to feed, excessive sleepiness, dehydration. Infants breathe mainly through the nose: a blocked nose can be serious.
Mergi urgent la stomatolog/medic dacă ai: See a dentist/doctor urgently if you have: swelling of the face or neck, fever, difficulty swallowing or opening the mouth, an abscess, pain radiating into the arm/jaw with sweating (it may be cardiac), pain after trauma.
Meridianele (jingluo) sunt, în tradiția: The meridians (jingluo) are, in the TCM tradition, channels through which Qi circulates. The twelve main meridians bear the names of the Zang-Fu organs: Lung (LU), Large Intestine (LI), Stomach (ST), Spleen (SP), Heart (HT), Small Intestine (SI), Bladder (BL), Kidney (KI), Pericardium (PC), Triple Burner (TE), Gallbladder (GB) and Liver (LR). To these are added two important midline vessels: Du Mai (GV, along the line of the back) and Ren Mai (CV, on the front of the trunk). The codes are the WHO ones, which you will always use.
Meridianele nu sunt structuri anatomice: Meridians are not identified anatomical structures; the clock has no experimental support as a physiological phenomenon.
Meridianele principale, cuplările yin–ya: The main meridians, the yin–yang pairings and the meridian clock
Meridianele sunt un concept tradițional;: Meridians are a traditional concept; imaging and dissection have not demonstrated dedicated anatomical structures.
Meridianele yang ale brațului (LI, SI, T: The yang meridians of the arm (LI, SI, TE) run from the hand toward the head.
Meridianele yin ale piciorului (SP, KI,: The yin meridians of the leg (SP, KI, LR) ascend from the foot toward the chest.
Meridianele yin și yang sunt cuplate: LU: The yin and yang meridians are coupled: LU–LI, ST–SP, HT–SI, BL–KI, PC–TE, GB–LR.
Meridianele și Qi-ul nu sunt structuri a: Meridians and Qi are not identified anatomical structures; modern explanations invoke neural and neurochemical mechanisms.
Meridianul stomacului are 45 de puncte,: The stomach meridian has 45 points, from ST1 (below the eye) to ST45 (second toe).
Mers regulat, exerciții de întărire a cv: Regular walking, quadriceps strengthening exercises, weight loss if needed, suitable footwear, heat for stiffness, avoiding deep squats.
Mers ușor, evită stat prelungit pe scaun: Gentle walking, avoid prolonged sitting, gentle stretches of the back and thigh, frequent changes of position, local heat, correct lifting of weights.
Mese mai mici și mai rare, mestecat lent: Smaller and less frequent meals, slow chewing, avoid alcohol, smoking and late meals, a light walk after meals, stress reduction.
Mese mici și dese, biscuiți uscați înain: Small and frequent meals, dry crackers before getting up, ginger, hydration, avoiding strong smells, rest; discuss safe options with the doctor.
Mese mici și dese, evită mirosurile pute: Small and frequent meals, avoid strong smells and fatty foods, hydrate with small sips, ginger, fresh air.
Mese mici, nu te întinde 2–3 ore după ma: Small meals, do not lie down for 2–3 hours after eating, raise the head of the bed, avoid alcohol, coffee, fatty meals and smoking, lose weight if needed.
Mestecat lent, evită băuturile acidulate: Chew slowly, avoid fizzy drinks and eating in a hurry, a short walk after meals, mint or fennel teas, notice the foods that bother you.
Meta-analiza sintetizează statistic date: A meta-analysis statistically combines data from several studies, providing a more stable estimate.

Migrenă, durere de tâmplă, trismus, dure: Migraine, temple pain, trismus, jaw pain
Migrenă, durere laterală de gambă și de: Migraine, lateral leg and rib pain, joint pain
Migrenă, tinitus, durere de coaste, dure: Migraine, tinnitus, rib pain, eye pain
Mingea de tenis pe perete pentru spate: Tennis ball against the wall for the back
Mingea, rola și covorașul permit presiun: The ball, roller and mat allow pressure on hard-to-reach areas, using body weight.
Mingea: așază-te cu spatele pe un perete: The ball: sit with your back against a wall or on the floor and place the ball beside the spine (not on the spine), at the level of points BL13–BL17 or BL23. Let your body weight provide the pressure, hold for 30–60 seconds, then move slightly. For the buttocks, the ball on point GB30 is a classic. The foam roller is better for large muscles (thighs, lower back) by slow rolling, but do not roll directly over the low back region if it hurts.
Mișcare aerobă blândă (mers, înot, tai-c: Gentle aerobic exercise (walking, swimming, tai chi), a regular sleep schedule, stress management, warm-up before exertion, gradual pacing of activities.
Mișcare regulată, somn suficient, reduce: Regular exercise, enough sleep, reduced caffeine, breaks, diaphragmatic breathing, conversations with trusted people, psychological counseling if needed.
Mișcare ușoară regulată (mers, înot), ev: Regular light exercise (walking, swimming), avoiding prolonged bed rest, breaks to get up from the chair every 30–45 minutes, local heat, sleeping on a sufficiently firm mattress.
Mișcări ascendente și spre exterior, făr: Upward and outward movements, without pulling the skin
Mișcări rapide de intrare–ieșire (varian: Rapid in–out movements (a variant described in the literature as "fast-in, fast-out") or retention for 5–15 min
Mobilizarea articulațiilor (tracțiuni, r: Joint mobilization (traction, rotations) only by trained practitioners
Mobilizarea zonei durerii în timpul trat: Mobilizing the painful area during treatment
Moderate pentru indicațiile clasice (dur: Moderate for the classic indications (chronic pain, migraine, nausea).

Modularea semnalelor nervoase ale dureri: Modulation of nerve pain signals and release of substances such as endorphins.

Moxibustion warms; avoid it in high fever.

Moxă (țigară, indirectă), compresă caldă: Moxa (stick, indirect), warm compress, infrared lamp
Moxă fină (Artemisia argyi), bețișor de: Fine moxa (Artemisia argyi), incense stick, ash container

Multe culturi au dezvoltat sisteme de ma: Many cultures have developed systems of therapeutic massage with pressure on points or lines. They clearly resemble acupressure, but differ in history, theory and style. We will compare four: Tuina (China), Shiatsu (Japan), Nuad Thai (Thailand) and Marma (India, Ayurveda).
Multe zone sunt sensibile fără legătură: Many areas are tender without any connection to classic points. Pressure should remain comfortable.
Munca la calculator înseamnă ore în acee: Computer work means hours in the same position: head forward, shoulders raised, fixed gaze. Self-acupressure does not correct posture, but it can reduce muscle tension and can be a useful break between work periods. It works best together with movement, hydration and regular breaks.
Mâini, ulei sau pudră, uneori bețe de le: Hands, oil or powder, sometimes wooden sticks
Mâinile curate, unghiile scurte; poziție: Clean hands, short nails; stable, relaxed position (seated or lying down).
Mâinile practicantului; uneori uleiuri s: The practitioner's hands; sometimes herbal oils or ointments
Mâna este considerată o hartă a corpului: The hand is considered a map of the body (microsystem), with 14 "small" meridians and points corresponding to the organs; fine needles, magnets or pressure are used.
Mâncărimi genitale, tulburări de menstru: Genital itching, menstrual disorders, urinary retention, leg pain
Mărimea efectului arată cât de mare este: Effect size shows how large the difference is, not only whether it is "statistically significant". An effect can be certain (small p) yet unimportant to the patient. Mean differences on pain scales (for example 0–10), standardized differences (where 0.2 is small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large) and the minimal clinically important difference are used. In the synthesis by Vickers et al. (2018, J Pain), using individual data from 39 trials, acupuncture was better than no treatment by a larger difference and better than sham by a small difference, which shows that part of the benefit is contextual.
Mărimea efectului contează mai mult decâ: Effect size matters more than statistical significance alone.
Măsoară-ți cu degetele 1 cun (lățimea po: Measure with your fingers 1 cun (the width of the thumb at the joint) and 3 cun (four fingers). Then, on your own forearm, find with a dermatographic pencil or with your finger a point 2 cun above the wrist crease, on the inner side, between the two tendons visible when you clench your fist. Press gently, without pain. This is the landmark for PC6.
Măsurarea conductanței pielii pe puncte: Measurement of skin conductance at points (Ryodoraku points) to assess the balance between meridians and guide treatment. Reproducibility results are limited.
Măsurarea la 24 de puncte pe mâini și pi: Measurement at 24 points on the hands and feet
Măsurarea rezistenței electrice a pielii: Measurement of the skin's electrical resistance at points, interpreted as the "state of the organs", and treatment by "frequencies". Controlled studies do not confirm its validity.
NICE NG59 — lombalgie și sciatică (recom: NICE NG59 — low back pain and sciatica (recommendation 1.2.8) —

Nas înfundat, rinită, sinuzită, paralizi: Stuffy nose, rhinitis, sinusitis, facial paralysis.
Neijing (Canonul Intern) cuprinde Suwen: The Neijing (Inner Canon) comprises the Suwen (Basic Questions) and the Lingshu (Spiritual Pivot).

Neuropatia scade sensibilitatea la căldu: Neuropathy reduces sensitivity to heat, so burns may go unnoticed.
Nevoie urgentă și frecventă de urinare,: Urgent and frequent need to urinate, sometimes with leakage, without an active infection.

They have not been identified as distinct anatomical structures, but their map remains useful as a language of localization.

Nu există dovezi că acupresura accelerea: There is no evidence that acupressure speeds up the healing of an infection; it may be only a relaxation routine during recovery.
Nu există dovezi că acupresura tratează: There is no evidence that acupressure treats constipation in children; gentle abdominal massage may be only a relaxation routine alongside dietary measures.
There is no evidence that acupressure treats infectious diarrhea; hydration is essential. Massage and warmth may offer only comfort.
There is no evidence that acupressure treats growing pains; gentle massage can soothe the child, but have serious causes ruled out by a doctor.
Nu există dovezi pentru acupresura la co: There is no evidence for acupressure in children with a stuffy nose; the priorities are clearing the nose and monitoring. Gentle massage is only comfort.
Nu există dovezi pentru acupresura în di: There is no evidence for acupressure in teething discomfort; the basic measures are the comfort measures described under self-care.
Nu există dovezi solide că acupresura am: There is no solid evidence that acupressure relieves cough; it can be used as a relaxation measure. A persistent cause must be investigated.
Nu există dovezi solide că acupresura sc: There is no solid evidence that acupressure shortens a cold; it may ease the sensation of nasal congestion and improve comfort.
Nu există dovezi solide pentru acupresur: There is no solid evidence for acupressure for children's sleep; the gentle massage ritual is mainly a relaxation and bonding routine.
Nu există dovezi solide; sughițul trecăt: There is no solid evidence; transient hiccups usually go away on their own, and acupressure may be a method of distraction and breathing.
Nu există studii solide specifice burnou: There are no solid studies specific to burnout; acupressure may help as a relaxation break, not as a solution to the causes of overwork.
Nu există studii solide specifice; autom: There are no solid specific studies; abdominal self-massage may bring comfort and relaxation, but does not correct the cause of bloating.
Nu pe oase fracturate, implanturi; evită: Not on fractured bones or implants; avoid vibration on inflamed areas.
Nu pe stimulator cardiac; poate irita pi: Not on a pacemaker; may irritate the skin.
Nu toate punctele sunt egale în tradiție: Not all points are equal in the tradition. Some have special roles, and knowing them helps in reading protocols. The Yuan (source) points are considered places where the organ's original Qi concentrates; on the yin meridians they usually coincide with the Shu point (for example LU9, HT7, KI3), while on the yang meridians they are separate (LI4, ST42, GB40). The Luo (connecting) points bridge the yin meridian and its coupled yang meridian; examples: LU7, PC6, ST40.
Nu tot ce se leagă de puncte este la fel: Not everything related to points is equally well founded. Classical acupuncture has studies, with mixed results; other practices look scientific but lack evidence. Recognizing the difference is a skill.
Nu în febră, tromboză, osteoporoză sever: Not in fever, thrombosis, severe osteoporosis, recent fractures; caution in pregnancy (key areas). Serious cases (thrombosis, embolism) have been rarely reported.

Nu întrerupe medicamentele fără acordul: Do not stop medication without your doctor's approval.

Pe lângă cun, punctele se găsesc folosin: Besides the cun, points are found using anatomical landmarks: bony prominences (malleolus, radial styloid), skin creases (the wrist crease), tendons visible on movement, palpable depressions. Many of the classic points feel like small hollows or slightly tender areas. Tenderness to pressure is a clue, but not a reliable criterion: many areas are tender without any connection to a classic point.

Pentru durerea ATM acupunctura are dovez: For TMJ pain acupuncture has limited evidence; massage and relaxation can help, but dental treatment remains the basis.
Pentru durerea cervicală acupunctura și: For neck pain, acupuncture and massage have limited to moderate evidence of short-term relief; acupressure mainly brings muscle relaxation and comfort.
Pentru durerea de umăr există dovezi lim: For shoulder pain there is limited evidence that acupuncture helps in the short term; acupressure remains a comfort adjunct, not a treatment for the injury.
Pentru durerea dentară postoperatorie ac: For postoperative dental pain acupuncture has limited evidence; acupressure may offer only a temporary comfort effect and does not treat the cause.
Pentru dureri musculo-scheletice există: For musculoskeletal pain there are weak signals, but many studies are of low quality.
Pentru greață postoperatorie, stimularea: For postoperative nausea, stimulation of PC6 (including acupressure) has low-quality evidence versus sham and moderate-quality evidence of equivalence with antiemetics (Cochrane 2015); for chemotherapy-related nausea a 2023 meta-analysis shows benefits, but the studies are few and heterogeneous; evidence is limited for fatigue, anxiety and pain.
Pentru oboseala nespecifică dovezile sun: For nonspecific fatigue the evidence is limited; some studies show short-lived improvements with acupressure (for example in chronically ill patients), but the quality is modest.
Pentru ochi se apasă doar pe osul din ju: For the eyes, press only on the bone around the orbit, never on the eyeball.

Placebo este un tratament fără mecanism: A placebo is a treatment without an active mechanism, which can nevertheless improve symptoms through expectation, attention and context. In acupuncture, "sham" (simulation) is used: needles that do not penetrate (Streitberger retractable needles) or needling at "wrong" points. The problem: sham acupuncture can also stimulate the skin, so it may have an effect of its own. If the difference between real acupuncture and sham is small, there are two interpretations: either the exact point does not matter much, or it does, but the sham is not inert. That is why several types of comparison are useful: acupuncture vs. sham, vs. no treatment and vs. standard treatment.
Placebo poate reduce simptome (mai ales: Placebo can reduce symptoms (especially pain), so trials need a control group.

Presiune cu palmele pe puncte: Pressure with the palms on points

Presiune lentă până la „durere suportabi: Slow pressure up to "bearable pain" (6–7 out of 10)

Moderate pressure for 30–60 s on the points on the foot and the lumbar area, 1–2 times a day, as an adjunct to bladder training. In pregnancy omit SP6.
Presiune medie 60 s pe fiecare punct, cu: Moderate pressure for 60 s on each point, with slow breathing, once a day, especially in the evening. Avoid painful pressing.
Presiune pe linii de la picioare spre șo: Pressure along lines from the legs toward the hips, then the back, arms, neck
Presiune pe puncte-cheie (ST36, GB20, LI: Pressure on key points (ST36, GB20, LI4)
Presiune perpendiculară, lentă, cu greut: Perpendicular, slow pressure, with body weight, 3–10 s per point
Presiune sau ac fin în punct: Pressure or a fine needle in the point

Presiune ușoară și mișcări pe puncte ale: Light pressure and movements on facial points (ST2, LI20, GB14, GV24) for muscle relaxation and local circulation; frequently used with a jade or quartz roller.
Presiune ușoară și pansament dacă este n: Light pressure and a dressing if needed
Presiune ușoară-medie 30–60 s pe punctel: Light-to-moderate pressure for 30–60 s on the points around the ear, without inserting fingers into the ear. It can be combined with relaxation and background sound.
Presiune și durere în zona frunții și ob: Pressure and pain in the forehead and cheek area, with a stuffy nose, usually after a cold or allergy.
Presiunea se aplică pe mușchii paraverte: Pressure is applied on the paravertebral muscles, not on bones, to avoid irritation or injury.
Presiunea se transmite întotdeauna direc: Pressure is always transmitted directly to the organ
Presiunea trebuie să fie fermă dar toler: Pressure should be firm but tolerable; warning signs require stopping.
Prima regulă a oricărei practici de sănă: The first rule of any health practice is to do no harm. Acupuncture with needles must be done only by qualified people, with sterile single-use needles. Serious risks are rare but real: infections, nerve or vessel injury, pneumothorax from incorrect needling of the chest or back, fainting. For this reason, in this course you do not learn to use needles and you are not asked to try anything of the kind at home.

Primele puncte Shu dorsale (ex. BL13, BL: The first dorsal Shu points (e.g. BL13, BL23) are located 1.5 cun lateral to the spinous processes.

Procedura are patru pași. Mai întâi găse: The procedure has four steps. First find the point: look for a small hollow or a slightly more tender area around the place indicated by the map. Then press perpendicular to the skin, increasing the pressure slowly over 3–5 seconds. Hold for 30–90 seconds, either static or with small circular movements of 1–2 mm. At the end, release as slowly as you went in. You can repeat 2–3 times per point, alternating sides of the body.

Procedură de control („acupunctură place: Control procedure ("placebo acupuncture") in trials: non-penetrating needle or inappropriate points.

Protocoale pentru greață, cefalee de ten: Protocols for nausea, tension headache, insomnia and stress
Protocol rapid de 5 puncte auriculare (c: Quick protocol of 5 auricular points (cingulate gyrus, thalamus, omega 2, point zero, Shenmen), with semi-permanent needles, for acute pain.
Protocolul Cochrane 2025 pentru migrenă: The 2025 Cochrane protocol for migraine has no results yet.
Prurit și afecțiuni cutanate, durere de: Pruritus and skin conditions, knee pain, urticaria.
Puls și limbă sunt cele mai cunoscute: t: Pulse and tongue are the best known: the tradition describes numerous pulse types (rapid, slow, thready, wiry) and tongue features linked to patterns. Pulsul și limba sunt centrale în MTC, da: The pulse and the tongue are central in TCM, but their reliability as an independent test is limited.

Punctele Huatuojiaji sunt paravertebrale: The Huatuojiaji points are paravertebral, 0.5 cun lateral to the spine.
Punctele Shu dorsale (de exemplu BL13, B: The dorsal Shu points (for example BL13, BL15, BL18, BL20, BL23) are on the back. Those on the front are the Mu points.
Punctele Xi (de fisură) sunt locuri în c: The Xi (cleft) points are places where Qi and blood "gather" in depth and are traditionally used for acute or painful states of the respective organ (for example LU6, PC4, ST34). Randomizarea și alocarea ascunsă reduc d: Randomization and concealed allocation reduce systematic differences between groups.
Rațiunea MTC (Qi) și cea modernă (răspun: The TCM rationale (Qi) and the modern one (nervous response, relaxation) are different explanations, not evidence for each other.
Reducerea intensității la zero înainte d: Reducing the intensity to zero before releasing the clips and removing the needles
Reducerea mișcărilor repetitive, exerciț: Reducing repetitive movements, stretching and eccentric strengthening exercises guided by a physiotherapist, ice for 10 minutes after exertion, ergonomics for the mouse and tools. In pregnancy omit LI4.
Reflexologia plantară aplică presiuni pe: Foot reflexology applies pressure to areas of the soles, according to certain maps.
Reflexologia plantară și palmară porneșt: Foot and hand reflexology starts from the idea that areas of the sole or palm correspond to organs. Practitioners massage the "reflex zones". Historically, the idea spread in the West in the 20th century (William Fitzgerald, Eunice Ingham). Studies generally show that reflexology may reduce anxiety and increase comfort, but there is no robust evidence that diagnosing diseases from the sole is possible or that it treats diseases of the internal organs. Reflexologia: dovezi pentru relaxare și: Reflexology: evidence for relaxation and comfort, not for diagnosis or treating the organs.
Reglarea organelor pe spate: Regulating the organs on the back
Regula 20-20-20 (la 20 min privește 20 s: The 20-20-20 rule (every 20 min look 20 seconds at something 6 meters away), conscious blinking, good lighting, lubricating drops on a doctor's recommendation, periodic eye examination. In pregnancy omit LI4.
Regula generală: cu cât o variantă este: The general rule: the more invasive a variant is (needles, incisions, injections, fire), the more you need a qualified practitioner, sterile material and information about the risks. No variant replaces a medical diagnosis.
Relaxare facială, tensiune de maxilar, c: Facial relaxation, jaw tension, tension headache
Relaxare, stres, tensiune; auto-aplicare: Relaxation, stress, tension; self-application for the hands and fingers (JSJ)
Relații complementare și tipare dinamice: Complementary relationships and dynamic patterns of balance.
Ren Mai (CV) merge pe linia mediană a ab: The Ren Mai (CV) runs along the midline of the abdomen and chest, from the perineum to the mentolabial groove.

Reston, de la New York Times, a descris: Reston, of the New York Times, described the treatment of postoperative pain with acupuncture.

Retenție urinară, edem abdominal, dureri: Urinary retention, abdominal edema, menstrual pain.

Rezerva științifică este clară: meridian: The scientific reservation is clear: meridians have not been identified as distinct anatomical structures. Studies that looked for channels visible through imaging or tracers gave inconsistent and unconfirmed results. The meridian clock has no experimental support as a physiological phenomenon; real circadian rhythms exist, but they follow other patterns. In other words, the clock is a mnemonic tool and a cultural convention, not a biological fact.
Rețeaua meridianelor (Jing) și a colater: The network of meridians (Jing) and collaterals (Luo) through which Qi circulates.

Yang is associated with activity, heat, the exterior, the upper part and the back of the body; Yin with rest, coolness, the interior, the lower part and the front. Neither exists without the other, and health is seen as dynamic balance, not a fixed point. It is a language of relationships, used to describe patterns: a person with "cold" and fatigue is described differently from one with "heat" and agitation.
Yintang se află la mijlocul distanței di: Yintang is located midway between the two eyebrows.
Yin–Yang descrie relații complementare ș: Yin–Yang describes complementary relationships and patterns, not two substances.
Yin–Yang este un limbaj al relațiilor: a: Yin–Yang is a language of relationships: activity and rest, hot and cold, exterior and interior, in a dynamic balance.
Yuan = punct sursă; Luo = punct de legăt: Yuan = Source point; Luo = Connecting point between the yin meridian and its coupled yang meridian; Xi = Cleft point, traditionally used for acute conditions.
Zang sunt organele „pline” (yin), Fu sun: Zang are the "full" (yin) organs, Fu are the "hollow" (yang) organs.
Zang-Fu este numele tradițional pentru „: Zang-Fu is the traditional name for the internal "organs" in TCM. The Zang are the "full" or yin organs (Liver, Heart, Spleen, Lung, Kidney, plus the Pericardium), considered storehouses of vital substances. The Fu are the "hollow" or yang organs (Gallbladder, Small Intestine, Stomach, Large Intestine, Urinary Bladder and the Triple Burner), which receive, transform and eliminate. By convention, we capitalize the names so as not to confuse them with the anatomical organs.
Zang-Fu se referă la funcții ale sistemu: Zang-Fu refers to functions of the system, not to anatomical organs in the strict sense.
Zang-Fu sunt sisteme funcționale, nu org: Zang-Fu are functional systems, not anatomical organs as in Western medicine.

În MTC, Inima adăpostește Shen: conștiin: In TCM, the Heart houses the Shen: consciousness, mental clarity and sleep.
În MTC, Qi (se citește aproximativ „ci”): In TCM, Qi (pronounced roughly "chee") is the central idea. It is described as a vital activity that moves, warms, defends and transforms. It is not a measurable substance in the physical sense, but an explanatory concept: a scheme by which traditional physicians organized observations about energy, digestion, breathing or resistance to illness. When we say "in the TCM tradition, Qi is blocked," we are describing a model, not a structure we have seen under a microscope.
În România, practicile complementare sun: In Romania, complementary practices are covered by Law 118/2007. According to some sources, acupuncture is practiced by physicians, dentists or pharmacists with attested competence, but the implementing rules were absent for a long time, and in 2025 the supreme court ordered the Ministry of Health to issue them. We cannot guarantee the up-to-date situation here: check the legislation in force and ask the practitioner what qualification they have.

În jurul acestor două metode există o fa: Around these two methods there is a broad family of variants. Some keep the needle but change the stimulus: electroacupuncture passes a weak current through the needles, and auricular acupuncture works on the outer ear. Others use heat (moxibustion, with burned mugwort), vacuum (cupping), friction or pressure (gua sha, tuina massage, shiatsu) or modern devices (low-intensity laser, transcutaneous electrical stimulation). There are also movement and breathing practices, such as qigong, which belong to the same medical culture but are no longer "point techniques."

Cea mai veche sursă clasică a medicinei: The oldest classical source of Chinese medicine is the Huangdi Neijing ("Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon"), a collection of texts assembled in layers between the Warring States period and the Han dynasty (approximately the 4th–1st centuries BCE; the exact dating is disputed). The current form of the Suwen is based on a commented edition from the 8th century (Wang Bing). It has two main sections, the Suwen ("Basic Questions") and the Lingshu ("Spiritual Pivot"), presented as dialogues between the emperor and his physicians. The Lingshu describes needles, meridians and needling techniques. The text is not the work of a single author, and its attribution to a mythical emperor is a literary convention.

Din China, practica a călătorit spre est: From China, the practice traveled east. Via Buddhist and diplomatic routes it reached Korea and Japan in the first centuries CE (in Japan, mainly from the 6th century), and there it acquired its own forms, for example the Japanese style, gentler, with very thin needles. In Europe, information arrived through Jesuit missionaries in the 17th century, and the Dutch physician Willem ten Rhijne wrote about acupuncture in 1683. In the 20th century, the French diplomat Georges Soulié de Morant popularized it in France. Western interest grew greatly after 1971–1972, when the American president's visit to China and a press report about a surgical operation drew public attention.

Durere cronică: sinteza lui Vickers și c: Chronic pain: the review by Vickers et al. (2018) found a modest effect versus sham and a larger one versus no treatment. The guidelines contradict each other: the American College of Physicians (2017) includes acupuncture among the non-pharmacological options for low back pain, based on low to moderate quality evidence, while the NICE NG59 guideline (2016) recommended that acupuncture not be offered for low back pain. A 2025 review of guidelines (Ho et al., BMC Complement Medicine and Therapies), on chronic musculoskeletal pain, found 17 guidelines and 35 recommendations, mostly weak or conditional, with a minority against. The message: there is no consensus.

Controlled studies have not shown that these measurements reliably distinguish people with and without allergies or other conditions; the device gives values that can be influenced by electrode pressure and skin moisture. These devices can lead to false diagnoses or unnecessary expense. Ryodoraku, a Japanese method of measuring conductance, raises similar questions about reliability.
